messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — new HF->Redwood conversion for the M7b fork is producing leading <pad> tokens in generation outputs after quantize step. Can repro locally.

liam: ugh. which conversion flags did you use?

maya: default hf_to_redwood.py from infra/tools, then our quant pipeline (ptq -> 4-bit). Steps: download, hf_convert, quantize. Example that repros in ~2s: 
```
# inspect tokenizer special ids
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
t = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('mistral-7b-fork', use_fast=False)
print(t.special_tokens_map)
print('pad_id', t.pad_token_id, 'bos', t.bos_token_id, 'eos', t.eos_token_id, 'unk', t.unk_token_id)
```
Result on the converted artifacts: pad_id=1 bos=2 eos=3 unk=4 but model logits treat id=0 as BOS in the original HF weights.

sara: do we have an added_tokens.json present? that's usually the culprit (ordering shifts IDs).

maya: yes — the HF repo had an added_tokens.json with an explicit order. After conversion our importer wrote those into the vocab front, shifting all IDs by +1. added_tokens.json snippet: 
```
["<pad>", "<s>", "</s>", "<unk>", "<special:role>"]
```
The model config.json claims `bos_token_id: 0`, but tokenizer ended up mapping `<s>`->1. So everything is off-by-one.

jonas: that explains why chat templates that rely on bos/eos are broken. The chat system emits BOS(0) but tokeniser's BOS is 1, so we see an unexpected pad at the start.

liam: can you diff the original HF vocab files vs the converted one? try `jq` on the JSONs.

maya: did that — quick diff: 
```
# hf vocab.json first entries
{"0": "Ġ", "1": "<pad>", "2": "<s>", ...}
# converted vocab.json first entries
{"0": "Ġ", "1": "<s>", "2": "</s>", ...}
```
So `<pad>` moved around.

qa-bot: detected regression: canary-test "chat-starter" latency OK but output tokens contain unexpected <pad> prefix. Failing 3/10 example prompts.

sara: Our importer should preserve special token ids if a model config explicitly sets them. The conversion tool currently reconstructs the vocab list from added_tokens in insertion order which is brittle.

jonas: temporary mitigation — add a conversion hook to remap token ids post-import: read config.json special ids and then write a `special_token_map.json` that maps old_id -> desired_id and update tokenizer files. Quick pseudo: 
```
# remap script idea
load config.json -> desired_ids
load tokenizer vocab -> current_map
compute perm such that token_with_name('pad') gets desired_ids['pad_token_id']
rewrite vocab.json, added_tokens.json accordingly
```
This keeps the binary weights untouched.

liam: also make quant pipeline assert that `tokenizer.pad_token_id == config.pad_token_id` and fail early. Add unit test in tests/model_onboard/test_special_token_alignment.py.

maya: i pushed a quick patch to infra/tools/hf_to_redwood.py in my branch `mg/special-token-fix`. It detects conflicting added_tokens order and prints a warning with remediation commands. Example output I added: 
```
WARNING: added_tokens order will shift token ids. Run: python scripts/fix_special_ids.py --config converted/config.json --vocab converted/vocab.json
```

liam: lmgtfy: also check `tokenizer.added_tokens_encoder` — some HF tokenizers use fast vs slow differences. Our converter was using `__call__` that reads the slow tokenizer only. Might be a fast/slow mismatch.

maya: good catch. I saw differences between `use_fast=True/False` during my local checks. I'll update the tool to prefer the HF `tokenizer_obj._build_special_tokens_map` when available.

qa-bot: Can we add a small acceptance test to the onboarding pipeline that does: encode('') -> first_token == bos_token_id and sample decode( [bos_token_id] ) contains expected marker? This should catch regressions before canary.

jonas: agreed. Also add a note in the model onboarding checklist: "verify added_tokens order + config special ids + quantized tokenizer parity".

maya: for immediate patching, i'm going to run the remap script and re-run canary. If it looks good i'll tag for a quick canary redeploy. Will post results here.

deploy-bot: deploy request created: canary/redwood/m7b-fork-remap @maya. Status: pending.

maya: canary after remap: 9/10 prompt samples fixed, one still shows trailing `<unk>` where we expect eos. Investigating mismatch between model's decoder eos handling vs tokenizer eos id.

liam: probably another off-by-one from a different added token set (rare emojis). Check `added_tokens.json` in both hf repo and converted artifact for extra entries.

maya: found an extra hidden token at the end of the HF added_tokens that was omitted by our converter, so the net effect was a two-step shift for some tokens. Fixing now.

sara: once this is stable let's add a small scripted audit that compares: len(vocab) + max(token_ids) + set(special_tokens) between HF source and converted artifact — quick parity checks.

jonas: long term: add `--preserve-special-token-ids` flag to the converter that refuses to reorder added tokens (or inserts placeholder tokens to maintain indices).

maya: will follow up with a PR for all the above. Thanks team. :raised_hands:

liam: thanks — great catch, nice debugging notes for future onboardings.

qa-bot: ticket created: ONBOARD-472 "HF->Redwood tokenizer special token id drift" assigned to maya, linked to canary artifacts.
